doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Tony Spargo, Bob Carter and Phil's complaint about swing playing
summary: Sidemen in Phil's Memphis Five, bassist Bob Carter regaining sight, and Phil objecting to four/four swing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: It was called the Memphis Five. It was a great band. But a funny thing is, we went up to Boston for two weeks and we played at Mrs. Donahue’s place, it was great, and he and I had a little falling out because he had Sol Yaged on clarinet, a young kid about 19 years old, Dick Brady on trombone, Tony Spargo on drums, who was fantastic. Did you ever hear that name?
From the old New Orleans Rhythm Kings, rhythm something.

Tony Spargo. His real name was Barbaro but he changed it to Spargo because everybody couldn’t say Barbaro. And Tony Spargo, he used to play the kazoo when he played a solo, and he would like he had a big Chinese crash cymbal. Boy he had great time. [scats] and man I used to jump off the stool, I said this guy’s great, I loved it. But anyway what happened was there was a bass player, his name was Bob Carter. Actually he had a long Hawaiian name, but he changed it to Carter because nobody could ever say his name, and he was blind. He had been temporarily blinded during the war. And I met him when he was working on 52nd street with Charlie Ventura and Bill Harris and they had a little group, and I got to meet him, we got to be good friends, and he’d say to me every time I met him, he recognize my voice and say “Marty, get me a gig, get me a gig.” So when Phil called me, when I was to rehearse with the band he said, “I need a bass player.” So I called Bob and I said, “hey Bob, I’ve got a gig for you.” He says, “get outta here.” And guess what, he says, “I got my sight back.”

I says, “you’re kidding.” He says, “yeah, it was a temporary thing, it was shock like.” But he says but there’s still a little thing in the center of his eyes that had to clear up yet see? I said, “beautiful, man.” So I got him on the band. But he was like a real [scats]. So I said but you’ve got to play two/four. He says, “I don’t care I’ll play anything.” So anyway he comes on the band, now we’re in Boston, we’re playing, and the band was just fantastic, it was a great Dixieland band, but every time a trombone solo, clarinet solo or piano solo, the guy’s like [scats]. So Phil says, “Marty, I want to talk to you.” So we went outside and we had a discussion on the sidewalk for about half an hour man. He was saying you know he went into an oration, a long one, about you know I didn’t make my name in

music without the fact that it’s jazz Dixieland because they love me because we play Dixieland, and you guys are playing four/four swing. And I said Phil, we’re not trying to disrespect you or anything. This is how we feel. We’re young guys and we like to play, I mean we’ll play what you want, we’re playing for you, don’t we — we went through a long, long thing and I finally convinced him I said, “we love what you’re doing, we love playing with the band. If it comes out that way we can’t help it, so what? How long does it last, a minute a half a minute? So he says yeah all right, okay, I don’t care what you play as long as it’s swinging like it is. And it got me off the hook see. And the band was just incredible, it was fantastic. So what happened was while we were there for those two weeks Mrs. Donahue was a beautiful lady, she invited us out to her house for dinner, and she said, “You guys like to golf?” I said, “I love to golf.” She says, “You got any clubs?” I said, “No, I’m on the road.” So Bob and I, he used to carry his clubs with him. We went golfing every day for two weeks, eight o’clock in the morning. When we finished the engagement I was paralyzed. Using muscles I hadn’t used. So we come back to New York and my wife had to wash my face, put my pants on. I couldn’t move. I was paralyzed. And now Phil called and he says, “We have to go and do two nights in Parris Island, North Carolina at the Marine place, you know that Parris Island? It’s a Marine place, where there’s Marines. Very famous. North Carolina. And we drove down there, and I drove with Bob in his car, all the way like this in the car. And he said, and I’m hanging on because my back is killing me, right? He says, “Incidentally, the doctor says even though I have my sight back, it could go off any minute.” So I says, “Thanks a lot, you shouldn’t tell me that while I’m in pain.”
You two guys were in great shape.
